### <samp>🤖 Generated by Copilot at 20f69b3</samp>

This pull request improves the layout performance and accuracy of various XAML controls by adjusting the metadata options of their dependency properties. It ensures that the controls update their layout when the properties that affect their size, position, or alignment change, and avoids unnecessary layout updates when the properties do not affect the layout. It also adds or modifies some properties to enable setting them in XAML and to trigger layout updates when they change. The changes affect the `Border`, `ContentControl`, `ContentPresenter`, `Control`, `DatePicker`, `Grid`, `Image`, `MediaPlayerElement`, `RelativePanel`, `SplitView`, `StackPanel`, `TextBlock`, `TextBox`, `ItemsControl`, `ItemsPresenter`, and `ScrollContentPresenter` classes, as well as the `DependencyPropertyMixins.tt` file.

comments.body: Hmm.. I don't think this should be affecting measure. But if that's what WinUI is doing let's follow that. I wouldn't expect this property to be changing dynamically that much in real scenarios, so doing the potentially unnecessary measure shouldn't be a problem.
This was intentionally not added. In `OnStrokeThicknessChanged`, we only invalidate measure if stroke is not null.

If we want to follow what WinUI is doing here, we should then delete the propertyChangedCallback.

@dr1rrb What are your thoughts?

The code in `OnTextWrapipngChanged` will end up invalidating measure anyways. This probably applies to other properties for TextBox as well.

Not sure if that will end up invalidating measure twice which in turn will cause measuring to happen twice?

It does according to this:

![image](https://github.com/unoplatform/uno/assets/1075116/2a6ef524-317e-46a0-bdc8-b5128970beb1)

It is interesting though, maybe they do the calculations for it in measure
Didn't catch that, good point! Can revert based on what you think
Afaik it shouldn't, the invalidation is just scheduled, so it should not cause trouble
I have no strong opinion as long as we keep one of `AffectsMeasure` and `OnStrokeThicknessChanged`. Will let @dr1rrb weigh on which one we should use.

The only effect here is that `InvalidateMeasure` will be called multiple times. In general, we have debouncing conditions where we won't be traversing the tree when asking for invalidation multiple times, so it should not be an issue. That being said, we may want to look for duplicates, particularly if they're done in the property changed handlers because the DP did not have the flag set.
This seems like a different type of change. In practice we should not have to invalidate the parent, but maybe the original commit will tell why it was there?

@jeromelaban It didn't work for me without that when I originally wrote this, and I haven't put enough time to understand why when I found this quite hacky way.

I was discussing this specific change with Martin. All we need is to verify that RTL checkbox still works as expected. If it does, then the change should be okay.

I think that we should not change at large options like this ... I suspect that there are lot of case where the `InvalidateMeasure` was done in the property change callback. For instance this case you can see that the `INvalidateArrnge` is invoked here https://github.com/unoplatform/uno/pull/14253/files#diff-7e87918895f8b453fa65dab2ed76539d91c6f5c9f896ef2962aaadd7af2e121aR243 after some check, and noticeably a feature flag for that ...

Yes I think that yes we should not cause an invalidate measure when we can prevent them like in this case where the `Stroke is null` ... even if cleaner to just have the flag on all properties, it will have a negative perf impact so I would keep the `OnStrokeThicknessChanged` callback.

Agreed, in such case I would still keep the flag there, commented out with an explainer why it is deliberately missing in our case, because it will make it easier to understand when we make changes in the future
`OnStrokeChanged` will invalidate measure only if necessary.
This is not an alignment with WinUI... on WinUI, the `Child` is not a dp! ;-)
It's unnecessary here as we do it in property changed through InvalidateTextBlock, but it doesn't harm as well

That was removed among the changes in this PR:

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6dad5f6a-c6ae-4e74-953d-b58f8e1909eb)

And instead, I added explicit `InvalidateMeasure` in callsites that were not coming from `AffectsMeasure` property changes (which was just a few locations)
However, I guess that could be kept, as it does not result in duplicate measure anyway and there is no location that needs `InvalidateTextBlock` without a `InvalidateMeasure` call
Ahh I see. Didn't notice it in the diff. I'll comment on that change separately
Very unimportant, but wanted to point it out. Foreground changes are doing InvalidateTextBlock but doesn't need to invalidate measure

I thought so too, but apparently on Android it the invalidation was needed - one of the tests started failing due to it missing - as the android native paint got invalidated only after the layout pass 🤔 . I could revert the last commit and adjust it to make the invalidation happen only on Android
I'm personally fine with the current approach
